title: The Future, And The Two Letters It Needed
label: ch:hi-bhavishya
canDo: I can say what I will do, what somebody else will do, and arrange to meet at a named hour.

payoff.summary: Read reading item 8 of the first practice paper word for word -- main panch baje aunga -- and answer the same question as a conversation at the aap level.
payoff.note: Closes two points and makes four scored mock items readable. HI-A1-V-11 wanted the future as a productive paradigm with agreement, and its note said milenge was taught as one memorised farewell rather than as a tense -- that half of the note is too strong and is corrected here: chapter 4 does take milenge apart, names the root, and states that Hindi marks the future with an ending rather than a helper word. What it gives is ONE CELL of a grid, the plural -enge, with no person and no gender, which is why the point was genuinely uncovered. HI-A1-T-06 wanted the adverbial baje, and its note is exactly right: chapter 18 teaches bajna as a predicate (ek baj raha hai, it IS one o'clock) and never the form that sits beside a number to fix a time to meet at. The chapter also pays down script debt: the independent vowels u, uu and o had never been taught anywhere in the track, and uu is what the whole first-person future waits on -- aaungaa and jaaungaa put a long u where no consonant can carry the mark, so it has to be written as a full letter.
